extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, research administrators, and other stakeholders in NIH grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page listing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource announcements relevant to preparing, submitting, and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate models for research (including NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of models that enhance human relevance and translational potential (including New Approach Methodologies), but emphasizes choosing the model best matched to the scientific question rather than adopting approaches for other reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and features
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH published a 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the PF5 overview to understand required application formatting, the award structure, and post-review splitting into linked awards so applications are prepared in the expected format and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 pilot format and include the specified simplified required elements rather than older or nonconforming formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability of biomedical research is foundational; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility and has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize such efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate replication/reproducibility considerations into study design, methods, and proposals; anticipate this highlighted topic in review and funding decisions and align proposals with NIH’s initiatives to increase reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND) review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who receive a CBND outcome should interpret it as being in the middle third of the study section (competitive but not discussed) under the adjusted procedures; consult NIH guidance/resources to understand implications for resubmission or administrative follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize centralization of NIH peer review within CSR and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR); NIH reports initial effects on efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review processes and timelines may be affected by CSR centralization and consider those effects when planning submissions and expectations around review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus and use NIH resources to stay informed
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Extramural Nexus is promoted as a source for the latest updates on grants policies, processes, and resources; readers are encouraged to subscribe for email updates, RSS feeds, and use posted resources (videos, data book, FAQs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staying subscribed and consulting Nexus posts, videos, the NIH Data Book, and FAQs helps applicants remain current on policy changes, application formats, deadlines, and other administrative requirements that affect grant preparation and management.
